scope: Passenger explicit STOP versus CBE-owned ordinary holds
findings: CortexPassengerReady native task deny list does not explicitly include STOP
CortexFlankEnd emits ordinary doStop and stores holders as actor membership, without an exact per-actor stop receipt
CortexRestoreCalm releases ordinary holder commands including STOP/ATTACK/FIRE/SUPPRESS using that membership; search-team cleanup has a separate stronger search-movement receipt
Calm remount and its bounded continuation use the shared passenger guard; an unconditional STOP denial could reject an owned hold that has not transitioned to follow yet
Convoy cover cleanup has its own destination-bound task record and must not be treated as interchangeable with ordinary holders
decision: Do not add a blanket STOP denial or an allow-STOP flag. First implement owner-local per-actor hold receipts across issuers, locality/checkpoint transfer and all return/cancel paths, then permit only exact current CBE-owned hold release before remount. Unknown/new mission stops must yield. Same-value external rewrites remain unobservable without controller cooperation.
required_next_work: Inventory all ordinary hold issuers and cleanup/rejoin/retreat paths
Bind stop receipt to original actor/group/owner epoch/native route and command identity, with finite lifetime and explicit acknowledgement
Recheck exact receipt at every native command boundary; preserve player/Zeus/actor-task ownership
Keep actual native switch/boarding observations separate from admission authority
Prepare normal and separate HC tests for owned holds, unknown STOP, new route, takeover, expiry, repeated remount and migration
